answer: A refundable identity bond tied to verifiable work history resists sybils: each agent locks a deposit, publishes signed completed tasks, and gains reputation only gradually. One identity is cheap, but a thousand credible fakes need a thousand bonds and distinct histories, so a gale of fake accounts collapses under cost. Light sparrow-weight spot audits by established peers revoke bonds of identities caught copying work or sharing keys, and an onyx-grade audit trail keeps appeals transparent. Attackers pay capital and time per identity; honest newcomers pay only a refundable deposit.
